channel.title: MurOS News
channel.description: Release notes and announcements for MurOS, the Debian-based firewall.

item.title: MurOS 0.9.92 released
item.description: The captive portal redirected every encrypted connection of an unauthenticated client to itself, whatever its destination. The client got a certificate warning for a site it never asked the firewall about, and the portal stayed hidden behind that warning. Only connections addressed to the firewall are redirected now, which is what a client detecting a captive network does. Plain web traffic between two clients of the same zone is no longer intercepted either, and the per-zone setting that hands the rules over to the operator is finally honoured.

item.title: MurOS 0.9.91 released
item.description: The rules the components register for themselves, the ones the rule page shows as automatically generated, were never applied. A DHCP server only answered if the operator had written the rule by hand, an IPsec tunnel only came up if IKE and ESP had been allowed by hand, and a captive portal could not resolve a name before authentication. They are now collected from the plugin tree and compiled into the ruleset ahead of the rules the operator wrote. The rule check also stops describing a rule left out for good as one waiting for a time window that does not exist.

item.title: MurOS 0.9.90 released
item.description: Applying the firewall replaced the entire nftables ruleset, which also took away the tables other parts of the system own. The captive portal keeps its authenticated clients and their traffic counters in one of them, so every reload disconnected the users of a portal zone and reset the volume they had consumed, which meant a data quota was never reached on a machine that reloads its firewall. The generated ruleset now replaces its own table and nothing else, in the same single transaction.

item.title: MurOS 0.9.89 released
item.description: NAT reflection, the last NAT feature the interface offered with nothing behind it, is implemented. A host on an inside network that asks for the published address now gets the same translation as one coming from the outside, with the return path translated so the answer comes back through the firewall. The release also fixes a rule bound to several interfaces, which resolved to none of them and matched every interface instead.

item.title: MurOS 0.9.88 released
item.description: An outbound NAT rule was translated from a fraction of what the page stores. The protocol, the ports, the translation pool and the address family were read by the interface and dropped on the way to the kernel, so a rule limited to one protocol translated everything, a rule pointing at a pool used the interface address instead, and a single IPv6 rule made the whole ruleset unloadable. Port forwards and 1:1 mappings now follow the address family too, and an address that cannot be resolved is left out and named rather than handed to the kernel as a host name.

item.title: MurOS 0.9.87 released
item.description: An alias that is not a list of addresses, a GeoIP country, a downloaded list, a host name, a MAC address, an autonomous system number, was emptied by every firewall reload. The old packet filter kept the contents of its tables across a reload and nftables starts from a flushed ruleset, so the rules using those aliases matched nothing for up to a minute. The resolved addresses are now written into the ruleset itself, and an alias that resolves to nothing at all is reported.

item.title: MurOS 0.9.86 released
item.description: Three features were still calling a program that does not exist on this system, and none of them failed loudly: exporting an OpenVPN client configuration produced an empty file, the cipher lists of the secure shell page were empty, and the flow collector attributed a flow to whichever interface happened to sit at that position in a list, so its reports were not empty, they were wrong.

item.title: MurOS 0.9.85 released
item.description: The traffic shaper can cap a download. A queueing discipline only works on what leaves a device, so the inbound half of a shaper rule silently did nothing; an intermediate device now carries it, with the same tree of pipes and queues as any other device. Measured between two namespaces, a pipe capped at one megabit stretched a burst of 1.1 megabytes from instant to 9.2 seconds.

item.title: MurOS 0.9.84 released
item.description: A pipe of the traffic shaper gets the queue it was configured with. The page has always offered the scheduler, the controlled delay targets, explicit congestion notification and the flow counts, and the port read none of them, so a pipe tuned against bufferbloat behaved like one left alone. What the kernel cannot express, including shaping what arrives on an interface, is now named rather than ignored.

item.title: MurOS 0.9.83 released
item.description: The table offenders are added to is filled again. A rule with a per source limit can name a table the sources that go over it are added to, which another rule blocks wholesale; the generator read the field and did nothing with it, so the block rule matched an empty table forever. Flushing the per source counters also does something now, the action was wired to a command that does nothing.

item.title: MurOS 0.9.82 released
item.description: A rule that asks for no connection tracking gets none, which matters for the traffic whose replies do not look like replies. And the options that cannot be translated at all are now named instead of dropped in silence: the rule check gained a verdict for a rule that is loaded but does not do everything it says.

item.title: MurOS 0.9.81 released
item.description: The quick option of a rule means something again. The older packet filter let the last match decide unless a rule was marked quick; a Linux ruleset stops at the first match, so the port had turned every rule into a quick one and a broad floating block written to be refined further down the list stopped everything it covered. The rules are now ordered so that the first match is the one the original semantics would have chosen.

item.title: MurOS 0.9.80 released
item.description: A firewall rule limited to a time window is limited again. The generator never read the schedule of a rule, so a scheduled rule was permanently active: a pass rule written to close at the end of its window never closed. Weekday sets, calendar days and hour ranges are honoured, and a rule outside its window is not loaded at all.

item.title: MurOS 0.9.79 released
item.description: A rule can now be checked against the kernel. Every silent failure found in this port had the same shape: an item accepted by the interface, stored, listed back, and never turned into a rule. The new check walks the configuration and separates a rule that is applied, one that waits for a reload, and one that will never be applied at all. Rule counters also work on the rules of the older pages now.

item.title: MurOS 0.9.78 released
item.description: The changelog tab of the firmware page shows something at last. A Debian package carries its own changelog, so the history up to the running version is already on the box, and the repository now publishes the changelog of every package alongside it, which lets a box read what a pending update contains before applying it.

item.title: MurOS 0.9.77 released
item.description: Wireless is driven through nl80211 instead of the FreeBSD ifconfig that no longer exists. The channel list, the transmit power table and the card capabilities come from iw, the status page shows the networks in range and the associated peers again, and an open network works: hostapd owns the beacon in every case, so an access point without encryption and a station joining an open network are both started as soon as a network name is configured.

item.title: MurOS 0.9.76 released
item.description: The source NAT rules written on the current GUI page are applied at last, with a masquerade for an interface target, a fixed address or a pool for the others. Also in this round: one-to-one NAT and IPv6 prefix translation on the nftables netmap statement, multi-WAN failover between the tiers of a gateway group including the connections already open, and per source connection limits on the firewall rules.

item.title: MurOS 0.9.75 released
item.description: Multi-WAN failover between the tiers of a gateway group, including the connections already open, one-to-one NAT and IPv6 prefix translation on the nftables netmap statement, per source connection limits on the firewall rules, host discovery on a packet socket, power savings mapped to the cpufreq governors, monit driving the Debian daemon, and the netstat diagnostics rebuilt on the Linux counters.

item.title: MurOS 0.9.41 released
item.description: Refreshed branding across the web UI, captive portal and installer, plus the usual round of fixes for the Debian platform.

item.title: Installer ISO updated
item.description: A fresh offline installer image is available from the download page. It ships the current MurOS build and needs no network access to install.

item.title: Getting started with MurOS
item.description: New to MurOS? The documentation covers installation, interface assignment and your first firewall rules.
